newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee ends lower on dlr demand from Calcutta.
newsitem.headline: India rupee ends lower on dlr demand from Calcutta.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended at 35.89/90 against the dollar on Tuesday, down from the opening level of 35.875/885, dealers said.
They said demand from an influential state-run bank in Calcutta helped the rupee close lower.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was not an aggressive dollar buyer on Tuesday, dealers said.
"They checked the levels and bought from whoever came to them," said a dealer at a private bank.
The RBI bought forward dollars of May and June maturities in outright transactions, dealers said.
The forward dollar premiums hardly moved on Tuesday. The six month annualised forward premium closed at 7.03 percent, marginally up from the previous close of 6.97 percent.
ICICI Securities and Finance Company said on Tuesday an overvalued rupee was hurting India's export competitiveness.
